q: What if all gold ever mined were melted into one cube?

brew.q: What if all gold ever mined were melted into one cube?

titles: All the Gold Ever Mined Fits in a Baseball Infield
Every Ounce of Gold in History, Melted Into One Cube
Humanity's Entire Gold Haul Is Smaller Than You Think

hooks.line: All the gold ever mined fits in an infield.
hooks.visual: Giant gold cube drops from the sky onto a baseball diamond, landing neatly between the bases with dust puffing out

hooks.line: Every gold bar in history. One cube. Guess how big.
hooks.visual: Stickman holds a measuring tape, staring up at a cube covered by a tarp with a big question mark

hooks.line: Five thousand years of digging. This is it?
hooks.visual: Timeline of tiny pickaxe stickmen from pharaohs to modern miners, all tossing nuggets onto one modest pile

hooks.line: The world's gold would barely fill a city block.
hooks.visual: Top-down map of a city block with a gold square inside it, plenty of space left over

hooks.line: Melt all the gold on Earth. Here's the shape.
hooks.visual: Rings, coins and bars pour into a glowing crucible that becomes a cube

beats.vo: Every bar of gold ever mined. One cube. It fits in a baseball infield.
beats.visual: Gold cube slams down onto a baseball diamond from above, crowd of stickmen in the stands gasps

beats.vo: Okay so. Humans have dug up gold for thousands of years. Pharaohs, empires, your aunt's wedding set.
beats.visual: Quick cutaways: pharaoh mask, Roman coin, stickman aunt flashing a gold bangle with sparkle
Bar chart in Money Moves style, a single gold bar labelled 216,000 t rising to the top of the frame

beats.vo: Melt it down: a cube about 22 metres per side. The infield is 27.
beats.visual: Crucible pours into a cube mould, then side-by-side diagram: cube 22 m vs infield square 27 m with dimension arrows

beats.vo: Stand next to it? Roughly a seven-storey building.
beats.visual: Stickman beside the cube, camera tilts up; a seven-floor apartment block slides in for comparison

beats.vo: Here's the wild part. At recent prices, that little cube is worth tens of trillions of dollars, in the same ballpark as the entire US economy's yearly output.
beats.visual: Price tag flips over the cube with spinning digits; chart shows gold cube value bar beside a US GDP bar of similar height
Zoom out to the stadium, the cube sitting smugly on the field, scoreboard reads GOLD 1 EXPECTATIONS 0

beats.vo: Nerd bonus: one cubic metre of gold weighs about 19 tonnes.
beats.visual: Single 1 m gold cube on a scale; the scale needle spins to 19 t and the scale cracks

beats.vo: And who owns it? Central banks hold only about a sixth. Nearly half is jewelry.
beats.visual: Cube slices into a pie chart: small vault-labelled slice for central banks, huge slice covered in necklaces and rings

beats.vo: Humanity's greatest treasure is mostly necklaces.
beats.visual: Stickman narrator sipping chai, deadpan, wearing an oversized gold chain

beats.vo: Everything we ever dug up. Still fits between the bases.
beats.visual: Back to the opening shot: cube on the diamond, a tiny stickman runner jogs around it to home

verify: Total above-ground gold mined: World Gold Council estimate of roughly 216,000 tonnes (end of 2024); update to the latest WGC figure
Cube side length: 216,000 t at density 19.32 g/cm3 gives about 11,200 m3, cube root about 22.4 m
Baseball infield: bases are 90 feet (27.4 m) apart, so the 22 m footprint fits inside the diamond
Seven-storey comparison assumes roughly 3 m per floor
Value: about 6.9 billion troy ounces times the current spot price; confirm it lands in the tens of trillions on publish day

US GDP comparison: US nominal GDP was roughly 29 trillion dollars in 2024; check that 'same ballpark' still holds at the current gold price (note: a stock compared with a yearly flow, framed as a size comparison only)
Central bank holdings: roughly 36,000 tonnes per WGC, about one sixth of the total
Jewelry share: WGC puts jewelry at roughly 45 percent of above-ground stocks; 'nearly half' should still be accurate
